en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty The Twelfth Chapter
The Discussion on Sound as Ripening:
Is sound ripening?
Yes, it is.
To be experienced as pleasant, to be experienced as painful, to be experienced as neither-painful-nor-pleasant;
associated with pleasant feeling, associated with painful feeling, associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling;
associated with contact, associated with feeling, associated with perception, associated with volition, associated with consciousness; having an object.
Is there for it turning toward, mental engagement, attention, volition, aspiration, and resolve?
One should not say so... [etc. ...

Is it not the case that it is neither to-be-experienced-as-pleasant nor to-be-experienced-as-painful... [etc. ... and is it without an object, such that there is no turning toward it... [etc. ... nor resolve?
“Yes.
“If it is not to be experienced as pleasant … [and so on] … if it is without an object, then there is for it no turning toward … [and so on] … no aspiration. Therefore, indeed, you should not say:
‘Sound is kamma-result.’”
Is contact a result; is contact to be experienced as pleasant … [and so on] … is it with an object; is there for it turning toward … [and so on] … aspiration?
Yes. Is sound a result; is sound to be experienced as pleasant … [and so on] … is it with an object; is there for it turning toward … [and so on] … aspiration? [Is this so?]
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Sound is a result;
sound is not to be experienced as pleasant … [as before] … it is without an object; there is no turning toward it … [as before] … nor aspiration? Yes.

“Contact is a result; contact is neither to be experienced as pleasant nor to be experienced as painful … [and so on] … it is without an object; there is no turning toward it … nor any aspiration for it?
One should not say this … [and so on] … It should not be said—
“Sound is a result of kamma”? Yes.
But was it not said by the Blessed One:
“Because that karma has been performed, accumulated, intensified, and expanded, he possesses the voice of Brahmā and speaks like the karavīka bird.
Is this indeed a sutta?
Yes, it is.
Therefore, sound is a result of karmic ripening.
The discussion on whether sound is a result of karmic ripening is finished.
